This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game studio. Then it explains the hardware behind
it. It ends with a **Do it** task (in a simulator, on the lab computer or on
your phone) and one set of questions. The full explanations, examples and
exercises are in the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary input-device output-device analog-input haptic-feedback gpu parallel-processing frame-rate refresh-rate thermal-throttling video-memory integrated-gpu graphics-card resolution >}}

## 3.1 How the player's action gets into the game

- An **input device** turns an action into numbers. The game reads them in
  every frame.
- **Touch screen:** the position of each finger, several at once.
  **Keyboard:** which keys are down. **Mouse:** movement and buttons.
  **Gamepad:** buttons, sticks, triggers. **Microphone:** sound.
  **Camera:** images.
- **Digital:** only on (1) or off (0): a key, the A button.
- **Analog:** a range of values: a stick from −1 to 1, a trigger.
- *Neon Drift* turns the car by 40° per second times the input. Key: 40°.
  Stick half way: 20°.

![Input devices send numbers in; output devices bring the result out.](images/io-devices.png){width=90%}

![A key gives 0 or 1; a stick gives any value from −1 to 1.](images/analog-digital.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The face buttons (A, B) of a gamepad are digital. Only the sticks and the
triggers are analog.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/input-lab.html" poster="sims/input-lab.png" title="Input Lab: what does the game read?" height="720" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Input Lab"}
Open **Input Lab** on your phone. How many fingers does your phone follow at
once? Drag the stick half way right and read "stick x". Press A and read
"button A". Which control is analog?

::: {.check}
A key gives only 0 or 1, so the car turns fully (40° per second) or not at
all. The stick gives values between −1 and 1, so the car can turn a little:
half way gives 20° per second.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Input"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the speaker|5"}
Which device sends the position of several fingers?
:   the touch screen

    Why: A touch screen reports every finger at once.

A key is down. Which value does the game read?
:   1

    Why: A key is digital: down is 1, up is 0.

A stick is pushed fully to the left. Which value does the game read?
:   −1

    Why: An analog stick gives −1 to 1; full left is −1.

The stick is pushed half way. The car turns 40° per second times the input. How far per second?
:   20°

    Why: 40° × 0.5 = 20° per second.

Which control can turn the car only a little?
:   an analog stick

    Why: An analog stick gives values between −1 and 1.
:::
:::

## 3.2 How the game talks back: output devices

- An **output device** turns data into an image, a sound or a vibration.
- **Display:** the picture. **Speakers, headphones:** the sound.
  **Vibration motor:** the player feels a crash (**haptic feedback**).
- Some devices are **both**: a touch screen, a gamepad with vibration, a
  headset with a microphone.
- Devices connect by cable (USB, HDMI) or without one (Bluetooth).
- A display has a **refresh rate** (Hz): pictures per second. The game makes
  **frames** (fps). The player sees only as many new pictures as the slower
  of the two.

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A normal monitor is output only. Its cable carries the picture out to the
player.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The devices around you"}
Open **Settings → Bluetooth & devices** on the lab computer and the
Bluetooth and sound settings on your phone (Android: **Sound and
vibration**; iPhone: **Sounds & Haptics**). List every input and output
device, built-in ones too. Mark each "input", "output" or "both".

::: {.check}
A good list has every device with its kind, for example: keyboard (input),
mouse (input), monitor (output), headset with microphone (both), phone touch
screen (both), phone speaker (output), vibration motor (output).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Input, output or both?"}
Choose the right answer. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match}
A monitor without touch.
:   output

    Why: It only shows the picture.

A keyboard.
:   input

    Why: It only sends key presses into the computer.

A gamepad with a vibration motor.
:   both

    Why: Buttons are input; the vibration is output.

The phone shakes when the car crashes. What is it called?
:   haptic feedback

    Why: A vibration you feel is haptic feedback.

A 60 Hz screen and a game at 70 fps. New pictures per second?
:   60

    Why: The screen shows at most 60 pictures per second.
:::
:::

## 3.3 Why games need a GPU

- One 1920 × 1080 frame has about **2 million** pixels. At 60 fps: about
  **120 million** colours each second.
- A CPU has a few strong cores (4 to 16). Good for long, different steps
  (game rules).
- A **GPU** has **thousands of small cores**. Each is slower, but all work
  at the same time on different pixels: **parallel processing**.
- Paint race (144 pixels): CPU with 4 cores 2.88 s, GPU with 144 cores
  0.32 s.
- CPU and GPU work at the same time on two frames: the slower one sets the
  frame rate.
- No fan in a phone: after some minutes the chip gets hot and slows down
  (**thermal throttling**).

![A few strong CPU cores and many small GPU cores.](images/cpu-gpu-cores.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A GPU is not a faster CPU. Each GPU core is slower. The GPU wins only when
the work splits into many similar pieces, like pixels.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/paint-race.html" poster="sims/paint-race.png" title="Paint Race: CPU or GPU?" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Paint Race"}
In **Paint Race**, press **Start the race** and write the two times. Why does
the GPU win, although each of its cores is slower?

::: {.check}
The CPU (4 cores) takes about 2.88 s, the GPU (144 cores) about 0.32 s. The
GPU wins because all its small cores colour different pixels at the same
time.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · CPU or GPU?"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the RAM|2 thousand"}
About how many pixels has one 1920 × 1080 frame?
:   2 million

    Why: 1920 × 1080 is about 2 million.

Which processor computes the colours of the pixels?
:   the GPU

    Why: The GPU draws the picture.

Which processor runs the rules of the game?
:   the CPU

    Why: The game logic runs on the CPU.

Many small cores work at the same time. What is it called?
:   parallel processing

    Why: That is parallel processing.

Is one GPU core faster than one CPU core?
:   no, it is slower

    Why: Each GPU core is slower; there are just many of them.

A phone game drops from 60 to 40 fps after 20 minutes. Why?
:   thermal throttling

    Why: A hot chip slows down to protect itself.
:::
:::

## 3.4 Video memory and graphics settings

- The GPU keeps textures and frames in **video memory** (VRAM).
- **Integrated GPU** (most laptops, all phones): part of the processor
  chip; it takes part of the main RAM (for example 2 GB).
- **Graphics card** (gaming desktops): its own GPU and its own fast VRAM
  (for example 8 GB).
- Textures that do not fit: the game stutters.
- **Graphics settings:** resolution (1080p ≈ twice the pixels of 720p:
  about half the fps), texture quality (more video memory), shadows and
  effects (lower fps).

![Integrated GPU and graphics card.](images/gpu-memory.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The GPU of the lab computer"}
Open **Task Manager → Performance → GPU 0**. Write the name of the GPU, the
**Dedicated GPU memory** and the **Shared GPU memory**. Is it an integrated
GPU or a graphics card? Why?

::: {.check}
A typical lab computer shows an Intel or AMD GPU with a small dedicated
memory and a large shared memory: an integrated GPU, because it shares the
main RAM. A graphics card shows several GB of dedicated GPU memory.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Video memory"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="on the SSD|nothing changes"}
Where does an integrated GPU keep its textures?
:   in the main RAM

    Why: An integrated GPU shares the main RAM.

The textures need 4 GB, but the GPU has 2 GB. What happens?
:   the game stutters

    Why: Textures that do not fit must be swapped: the game stutters.

A game runs at 120 fps at 720p. About how fast at 1080p?
:   about 60 fps

    Why: 1080p has about twice the pixels: about half the fps.

Which setting needs more video memory?
:   higher texture quality

    Why: Bigger textures need more video memory.
:::
:::

## Game challenge: tuning Neon Drift {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

*Neon Drift* must run at **60 fps or more** on three test devices of *Byte
Bay*. In this made-up game, 1080p halves the frame rate of 720p, and shadows
divide it by 1.5. Textures need 1 GB (Low), 2 GB (Medium) or 4 GB (High) of
video memory.

- **Laptop L1:** GPU inside the processor, 2 GB; 120 fps at 720p, shadows
  off.
- **Phone P1:** GPU inside the chipset, 2 GB; 90 fps at 720p, shadows off.
- **Desktop D1:** graphics card, 8 GB VRAM; 300 fps at 720p, shadows off.

{{< sim file="sims/settings-tuner.html" poster="sims/settings-tuner.png" title="Settings Tuner: Neon Drift on three devices" kind="game" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Laptop L1"}
Laptop L1: 2 GB of video memory, 120 fps at 720p with shadows off. 1080p
halves the fps; shadows divide it by 1.5. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="120 fps|4 GB"}
L1 at 1080p, shadows off. How many fps?
:   60 fps

    Why: 120 ÷ 2 = 60.

L1 at 720p, shadows on. How many fps?
:   80 fps

    Why: 120 ÷ 1.5 = 80.

L1 at 1080p, shadows on. How many fps?
:   40 fps

    Why: 120 ÷ 2 ÷ 1.5 = 40.

Which texture quality is the highest that fits on L1?
:   Medium (2 GB)

    Why: L1 has 2 GB: Medium needs 2 GB, High 4 GB.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Three devices (harder)"}
L1: 2 GB, 120 fps. P1: 2 GB, 90 fps. D1: graphics card 8 GB, 300 fps (all at
720p, shadows off). Goal: 60 fps or more. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Laptop L1|30 fps"}
Phone P1 at 1080p, shadows off. How many fps?
:   45 fps, too slow

    Why: 90 ÷ 2 = 45, below 60.

Phone P1 at 720p, shadows on. Is it enough?
:   yes, exactly 60 fps

    Why: 90 ÷ 1.5 = 60.

Which device can use High textures (4 GB)?
:   Desktop D1

    Why: Only D1 has more than 4 GB of video memory.

Desktop D1 at 1080p, shadows on. How many fps?
:   100 fps

    Why: 300 ÷ 2 ÷ 1.5 = 100.
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Input devices turn actions into numbers; keys are digital, sticks are analog.
- Output devices give an image, a sound or a vibration; the screen shows at most its refresh rate.
- The GPU uses thousands of small cores in parallel; the slower of CPU and GPU sets the frame rate.
- An integrated GPU shares the RAM; a graphics card has its own VRAM.
- Resolution, textures and shadows change the work of the GPU and the frame rate.
